metadata.title: Tesla Stock: Earnings Today Are All About a SpaceX Merger

content.text:
Oct. 21, 2026 at 9:54am ET
24 min ago
SpaceX might have stolen some of Tesla's thunder.
Elon Musk's rocket and AI company reported blowout third-quarter numbers last night. Beyond the financial figures, Musk shared important merger news. "Both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss [a merger] at the request of shareholders, and these special committees consist of independent directors," said Musk. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes."
Wall Street analysts and investors have speculated about a merger for months, for good reason. The most obvious reason is Musk, who heads both companies. Both companies are also betting their futures on AI. SpaceX is spending billions to build new AI data centers, which it is renting out for billions. Tesla is using AI to train cars to drive themselves and humanoid robots to complete labor-saving tasks.
SpaceX's AI growth, however, is way quicker than Tesla's. SpaceX's third-quarter sales were $14.6 billion, up 161% year over year. First-quarter 2027 sales are expected to be about $35 billion.
Tesla launched its robo-taxi service in Austin, Texas, in June 2025, but it has yet to contribute meaningfully to growth. Slower-than-hoped-for AI development is a big reason Tesla stock, entering Wednesday trading, is down about 17% this year.
Arguably, shares would be down more if not for the SpaceX merger mania. Barclays analyst Dan Levy recently wrote that his clients expect a deal announcement this year. RBC analyst Tom Narayan recently wrote that a deal price could be $480 a share. (SpaceX is seen as the buyer.)
Tesla's results will matter for the stock, but the EV maker's shares will be linked to SpaceX for the foreseeable future, no matter how many EVs the company sells.
